rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some object that predestination makes supplication futile: what is decreed will occur, while what is not decreed will not occur.
rows.anchor: duayı terk etmek evlâ olduğu bu vücûh ile sâbit olmaz mı? demeye kadar varanlar olmuştur

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: They argue that God already knows hidden intentions and circumstances, so prayer cannot inform Him and seems unnecessary.
rows.anchor: Hak sübhânehu allâmü’l-guyûbdur. Gözlerin hâin bakışını, sînelerin gizli tuttuğu niyetleri bilir.

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some cite Gabriel’s and Abraham’s surrendering sayings, acceptance of divine decree, and a sacred hadith preferring remembrance to asking to argue that leaving supplication is better.
rows.anchor: duayı terk etmek evlâ olduğu bu vücûh ile sâbit olmaz mı? demeye kadar varanlar olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overwhelming majority of rational people and scholars affirm that supplication is among the most important stations of servitude, supported by many rational and transmitted proofs.
rows.anchor: ukalâ ve ulemânın cumhûr-ı a‘zamı duanın ehemm-i makāmât-ı ubûdiyet olduğunda tereddüd etmemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predestination objection is incomplete: some outcomes are decreed conditional on supplication, just as satiety depends on eating and success on seeking and effort.
rows.anchor: Taleb ile, dua ile mukayyed olarak ma‘lûmü’l-vukū‘olan mukadderât vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created beings, not God, are subject to decree; prayer acknowledges divine precedence and is therefore a high form of worship.
rows.anchor: kadere mahkum olan Allah değil mahlûkāttır. Kaderler sâbık ise Cenâb-ı Allah da kazâ ve kadere sâbık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the secret of decree is unknown before it occurs, divine wisdom requires people to act between hope, which motivates success, and caution, which orders it; human duties remain valid.
rows.anchor: Yaşamak bu iki hasletin muvâzenesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since events are tied to causes and effort follows laws, supplication is itself one of the causes through which decreed outcomes occur.
rows.anchor: dua da o esbâbdan birisidir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Companions asked whether deeds were already settled or newly determined; the Prophet answered that they were settled, then commanded them to act because each person is eased toward what they were created for.
rows.anchor: Ashâb-ı kirâm Resûlullah’a cebr ü kader meselesini sormuşlar: “Yâ Resûlullah nasıl görürsün?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophetic answer preserves a middle position: neither absolute compulsion nor unrestricted freedom, but a balance of divine determination and human choice, with people facilitated rather than coerced.
rows.anchor: ve müsahhar değil müyesser buyurmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplication aims to display servitude and return in humility and abasement, not to inform God.
rows.anchor: Duadan maksud i‘lâm değil, izhâr-ı ubûdiyet, arz-ı zillet ü inkisar ile müracaattır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praying while accepting divine decree does not put human preference ahead of God; it magnifies divine power above all else.
rows.anchor: kazâ ve kaderine rızâ ile beraber Allah’a dua etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sayings attributed to Gabriel and Abraham are, fitting their station, eloquent forms of prayer; silent state can speak more eloquently than words for a sincere person in God’s presence.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i İbrâhim’in zikr olunan sözleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prayer need not state a request explicitly; direct speech, allusion, or an inwardly expressive state can each constitute supplication.
rows.anchor: Daha doğrusu dua sarih olduğu gibi kinaye ve îmâ ile de olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because praise to the Generous also contains supplication, a hadith calls praise of God the best supplication.
rows.anchor: bu sebeple أَفْضَلُ الدُّعَاءِ اَلْحَمْدُ للّٰهِّٰ buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Qur’anic passages command or commend supplication; the warning about hardened hearts shows that God is angry with those who do not turn to Him.
rows.anchor: Sonuncusu gösteriyor ki Allah istemeyenlere gazab eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fatiha had already been described as the Sura of Supplication and Teaching the Request, and as instruction in the etiquette of prayer.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Fâtiha’nın “Sûre-i Duâ” ve “Ta‘lîm-i Mes’ele” isimlerini de hâiz olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an gives fourteen question-and-answer passages, on foundational and practical matters; most use qul or faqul, with the prefixed fa signaling an immediate answer and delivery.
rows.anchor: Ekserîsinde قُلْ yerinde فَقُلْ buyurulmuştur ki, bu فا’da cevâbın müsta‘celiyetine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the other answers, God replies directly without saying qul or faqul, omitting the intermediary and expressing nearness through His promise to answer prayer.
rows.anchor: cevâbında doğrudan doğru فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ buyurulmuş, vâsıta hazf edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says “I am near,” rather than “My servants are near Me,” because a contingent creature cannot approach God by its own being; nearness comes from God’s side.
rows.anchor: kurbiyet taraf-ı abdden değil, taraf-ı Hak’dandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person occupied with anything besides God has not truly prayed; when absorbed in knowledge of the One and relinquishing personal claims, all intermediaries fall away and divine nearness is realized.
rows.anchor: dua eden kimsenin gönlü Allah’ın gayrısıyla meşgul olduğu müddetçe hakikaten dua etmiş olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the worshipper stops attending to personal interests and relinquishes all intermediaries, divine nearness becomes possible; surrender to God is fully realized.
rows.anchor: kendi hakkını mülâhaza ve nasîb-i beşeriyeti talepten imtinâ‘eder, vesâit bi’l-külliye mürtefi‘olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When self-interest is removed, surrender expressed in “I entrust my affair to God” appears fully; perception and desire become God-oriented, and divine will brings about what countless causes and centuries could not.
rows.anchor: milyonlarca esbâbın, asırlarca zamanların yapamadığı şeyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic hadith calls supplication the marrow of worship, supporting the author’s view that it is a means of nearness and among the best acts of worship.
rows.anchor: اَلدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ: dua ibadetin iliğidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another hadith defines worship as supplication and cites the command to call upon God and receive His response.
rows.anchor: اَلدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ: ibadet duadan ibarettir” diyerek ٱدْعُونِىٓ أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ âyetini okumuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who belittle supplication also belittle worship, fail to know God as near and responsive, and instead value the attention of creatures or take them as rivals.
rows.anchor: Dikkat edilirse görülür ki duayı mühimsemeyenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the fasting commands, God reassures the Messenger that He is near and answers those who call; this directs attention to supplication, especially in the state of fasting.
rows.anchor: İşte Cenâb-ı Allah bu babdaki bütün şüpheleri def‘ve ‘ibâdını irşad için duanın ehemmiyetine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants’ response should be wholehearted obedience to God’s commands; they should also believe Him and affirm what He has taught about fasting’s virtues, so that they may attain right guidance and their aims.
rows.anchor: onlar da Benim emirlerime candan icâbet ü imtisal etsinler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplication and command are requests in the same grammatical form: a needy person’s cry for help is a prayer, while the helper’s “get up” is a response and command.
rows.anchor: Mâlumdur ki dua ile emir, aynı sîga ile yapılan birer talebdirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater’s aid to the distressed is a mark of greatness; obedience to the greater is also required by good manners, reason, and the subjects’ own benefit, and rational action is called rushd.
rows.anchor: Muktezâ-yı akıl üzere harekete ise “rüşd” tâbir olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the absolute Greatest, present everywhere, able to meet every need, and nearer to people than they are to themselves; He explicitly promises to answer prayer.
rows.anchor: her yerde hâzır u nâzır, mahlûkātının her türlü hâcetlerini is‘âfa kādir ve onlara kendilerinden daha karîb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that those who believe in God and His rulings and obey them demonstrate sound reason and guidance, enabling them to reach their aims.
rows.anchor: ancak Allah’a ve ahkâmına îmân ile icâbet ü itâ‘at edenlerdir ki akl ü rüşdlerini isbât etmiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports the implementation of the fasting rulings and, by extension, all divine commands; fasting receives special emphasis because it seems especially difficult and contrary to appetite.
rows.anchor: Bu tevsîk ıtlâkıyla bütün evâmir ü ahkâma şâmil ise de bilhassa emr-i sıyâmı tâkip etmesi şâyân-ı dikkattir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı postpones the remaining details about supplication and returns to the discussion of fasting.
rows.anchor: O hâlde dua hakkındaki diğer tafsîlâtı gelecek olan diğer âyetlere bırakarak oruca devam edelim.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says early Muslims could eat, drink, and have marital relations only until the evening prayer or sleep, when fasting began; after ʿUmar did so after ʿisha and repented, others confessed similar conduct, and the following verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: bir gün Hazret-i Ömer yatsıdan sonra mübaşerette bulundu ve derhâl nedâmet edip huzûr-ı nebevîye geldi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command concerns Arab polytheists rather than People of the Book, as the wording about expelling them from where they expelled the Muslims indicates.
rows.anchor: وَأَخْرِجُوهُم مِّنْ حَيْثُ أَخْرَجُوكُمْ kaydı delâletiyle bu âyetin ehl-i kitab hakkında olmayıp Arab müşriklerine mahsus olduğu anlaşılır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Book could be accepted in submission through payment of the poll tax, while Arab polytheists were required to accept Islam or face the sword.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i kitâbın vergi ile mutâva‘atı dahi makbul olabildiği hâlde Arab müşrikleri ya İslâm veya seyfe mahkumdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here fitna means shirk and division; the fighting is to end those conditions.
rows.anchor: hatta fitne, yani şirk ü tefrika olmasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion being for God means that people submit and obey only God; since the true religion with God is Islam, no religion besides monotheistic Islam should remain among them.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki اِنَّ الدّ۪ينَ عِنْدَ اللّٰهِّٰ الاِْسْلَاَمُ’dır

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet said he was commanded to fight people until they profess that there is no god but God; then their lives are protected from him.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm “ben bu nâsa ‘lâ ilâhe illallah’ diyecekleri âna kadar kıtâle me’mûrum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other groups can gain protection by paying jizya, but permission for non-Muslims to reside in Mecca is also denied.
rows.anchor: Bundan başka bilhassa Mekke’de gayr-i müslimin ikāmetine müsaade de edilmemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Arab polytheists abandon unbelief and accept Islam, fighting hostility is directed only against wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: artık zâlimlerden mâ‘adâsına husûmet-i kıtâl yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hurumat are things whose preservation and respect are obligatory and which may not be violated; the term includes property as well as sacred months.
rows.anchor: Burada “hurmet”, muhafaza ve ihtirâmı vâcib olan, el uzatılması câiz olmayan şey demektir ki emvâle de şâmildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording first specifies sacred months, then generalizes the rule to all protected sanctities.
rows.anchor: Bu atıfta tahsisten sonra ta‘mîm vardır.

words: فَٱعْتَدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا ٱعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation is lawful only to the measure of the other party’s violation, as the principle that recompense for an evil is an equal evil states.
rows.anchor: onun size tecavüz ettiği kadar, yani misli olmak şartıyla siz de ona bi’l-mukābele tecavüz ediniz.

words: فَٱعْتَدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا ٱعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The maxim “the initiator is more unjust” identifies the first aggressor as the more blameworthy party.
rows.anchor: اَلْبَادِي أَظْلَمُ.

words: فَٱعْتَدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا ٱعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling equal retaliation “aggression” is verbal correspondence (mushakala); a normally ugly act becomes relatively good under the conditions that make retaliation a right.
rows.anchor: Buna tecavüz ve ta‘addî tâbir edilmesi, zât-ı fi‘ilde mümaselet dolayısıyla bir müşâkeledir.

words: فَٱعْتَدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا ٱعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Equivalence is essential: no retaliation is made when equivalence is impossible; seized property is returned if extant, replaced by a like item if fungible, or otherwise compensated at its value.
rows.anchor: Mümaselete riayet mümkin olmayan husûsâtta kısas yapılmaz.

words: فَٱعْتَدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا ٱعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only proportionate retaliation is permitted, not unrestricted counteraction; harm must be removed without inflicting a new, unequal harm, and equivalence is the means of removing it.
rows.anchor: meşrû olan mukābele-i mutlaka değil, mukabele bi’l-misldir. Misle riayet edilmeyince re’sen bir zarar îkā‘edilmiş

words: فَٱعْتَدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا ٱعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The maxim “no harm and no reciprocating harm” bars initiating harm and answering it with fresh harm; only equivalent redress removes the original injury.
rows.anchor: Re’sen zarar câiz değil, zarara zararla mukabele de câiz değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although qisas already entails equivalence, the verse restates equivalence to prevent neglect and emphasize that it is the rule’s intended condition.
rows.anchor: “kısas” kelimesi bu mümaselet mânasını mutazammın olduğu hâlde zühul edilmemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the general rule of equivalent sanctities, a prohibited month can be matched by the same prohibited month in response to violation.
rows.anchor: memnû‘ay da aynı memnû‘aya takas edilir.

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan reports that Arab polytheists asked the Prophet to forbid fighting in a sacred month; after he agreed, they broke the pact there, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan mervî olduğuna göre Arab müşrikleri Hazret-i Peygamber’e “Şehr-i haram’da kıtalden nehyetsen” demişler

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas, Rebî‘ b. Enes, Katâde ve Dahhâk
rows.claim: These authorities report that Quraysh expelled the Prophet, in ihram, from Mecca in sacred Dhu al-Qada at Hudaybiyya; the next year he returned for the compensatory umra as requital for that obstruction, occasioning the verse.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas, Rebî‘b. Enes, Katâde ve Dahhâk’tan rivayet olunduğuna göre Kureyş Hudeybiye senesi Resûlullah’ı ihramlı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Hasan’s report, the verse came before entering Mecca: it directly commands and implicitly promises the future response; on the other report, it came after entry and declares the return a requital while allowing fighting only when not initiated.
rows.anchor: evvelkine göre âyet Mekke’ye kable’d-duhûl nâzil olmuş, sarâhaten emr ü inşâ ve zımnen istikbâle ait va‘d ü ihbar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the verse’s context better fits the first occasion report.
rows.anchor: Siyâk-ı âyet evvelkine daha muvâfıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In either account, these verses were revealed in 7 AH during the Kaaba visit known as the Year of the Compensatory Umra.
rows.anchor: bu âyetler “Umre-i Kazâ Senesi” tâbir olunan hicretin yedinci senesinde ziyâret-i Kâbe sadedinde nâzil olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general ban on initiating war in sacred months was later abrogated by the Bara’a verses by consensus, while the general rule requiring equivalent retaliation remains in force by consensus.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin şehr-i haramda bidâyeten i‘lân-ı harbe cevaz vermeyen hükmü Berâe âyetleriyle bi’l-ittifak mensuhtur.
